problem_text:
A municipal water authority must devise a comprehensive strategy to curtail nutrient runoff from a network of agricultural drainage outlets. At present, no mitigation practices are in place.  
The baseline characteristics for each drainage outlet are detailed as follows:  
* For Outlet A, the nutrient leaching coefficient is 2.753, and the associated cultivated area is 173.281.  
* For Outlet B, the nutrient leaching coefficient is 2.763, and the associated cultivated area is 65.817.  
* For Outlet C, the nutrient leaching coefficient is 2.945, and the associated cultivated area is 158.669.  
* For Outlet D, the nutrient leaching coefficient is 1.93, and the associated cultivated area is 155.276.  
* For Outlet E, the nutrient leaching coefficient is 0.924, and the associated cultivated area is 171.058.  
* For Outlet F, the nutrient leaching coefficient is 1.452, and the associated cultivated area is 69.23.  
* For Outlet G, the nutrient leaching coefficient is 0.847, and the associated cultivated area is 112.925.  
* For Outlet H, the nutrient leaching coefficient is 1.253, and the associated cultivated area is 111.648.  

To address the nutrient load, several distinct best management practices (BMPs) can be implemented, each offering a specific capture efficiency:  
* Implementing Practice 1 will sequester 40% of nutrients.  
* Implementing Practice 2 will sequester 43% of nutrients.  
* Implementing Practice 3 will sequester 74% of nutrients.  
* Implementing Practice 4 will sequester 81% of nutrients.  
* Implementing Practice 5 will sequester 66% of nutrients.  
* Implementing Practice 6 will sequester 14% of nutrients.  
* Implementing Practice 7 will sequester 63% of nutrients.  
* Implementing Practice 8 will sequester 40% of nutrients.  

Adopting a practice at a given outlet incurs a fixed cost per unit of cultivated area. The cost matrix for all outlet–practice pairings is provided below:

| Outlet \ Practice | Practice 1 | Practice 2 | Practice 3 | Practice 4 | Practice 5 | Practice 6 | Practice 7 | Practice 8 |
|--|-|-|-|-|-|-|-|
| Outlet A | 162.775 | 72.613 | 73.6 | 164.94 | 173.307 | 195.103 | 35.864 | 70.926 |
| Outlet B | 189.983 | 48.162 | 69.695 | 193.269 | 194.058 | 65.375 | 142.042 | 103.291 |
| Outlet C | 119.417 | 56.061 | 81.451 | 165.134 | 84.658 | 31.639 | 117.132 | 122.523 |
| Outlet D | 113.67 | 139.525 | 114.519 | 191.071 | 97.708 | 144.59 | 93.306 | 65.353 |
| Outlet E | 141.639 | 165.603 | 161.175 | 87.737 | 104.868 | 130.334 | 55.984 | 135.146 |
| Outlet F | 145.895 | 159.925 | 24.053 | 198.233 | 101.055 | 86.153 | 106.256 | 184.875 |
| Outlet G | 141.425 | 113.293 | 160.237 | 78.311 | 180.145 | 112.012 | 131.254 | 26.147 |
| Outlet H | 156.101 | 134.944 | 77.452 | 132.93 | 18.416 | 196.886 | 138.72 | 85.927 |

The authority must decide which practices to deploy at each outlet (multiple practices may be applied concurrently to a single outlet), and it is permissible for an outlet to remain partially untreated. The objective is to guarantee that the total nutrient discharge is diminished by at least a fraction P = 0.576 of the baseline load, while minimizing the aggregate implementation expenditure.
